idiom_name: inherent associated functions (new, with_capacity, from_*) plus From/TryFrom and Default
implementation_notes: Rust has no constructors; a constructor is an associated function in an impl block following the API-guideline conventions - new for the primary route, with_* for alternative configurations (Vec::with_capacity), from_* for conversion constructors (String::from_utf8, u32::from_str_radix), and Default for the zero-argument route. Where the conversion is infallible and lossless, implement From/TryFrom instead so callers get .into() and the rest of the ecosystem's traits; the pattern's cache-or-subtype motive appears as constructors returning Box<dyn Trait> or Arc<Self>. The classic private-constructor structure is replaced by visibility: fields are private outside the module by default, which is what makes the named functions the only way in.
pitfalls: new is only a convention: a struct with public fields can be built by struct literal from another module, bypassing validation - keep the invariant-carrying fields private (a tuple struct with a private field does it in one line).
Fallible constructors must return Result<Self, E> instead of panicking or building a half-valid value; unwrap inside a from_* helper turns caller input errors into crashes.

A from_ constructor that duplicates an obvious From impl splits the API: the guidelines reserve from_ for conversions that are fallible, unsafe, or need extra arguments (Box::from_raw, u64::from_str_radix).
